Ability to work effectively across scientific, regulatory, quality, marketing, commercial, and technical functions. Ability to independently manage assigned projects while contributing effectively within cross-functional teams. Strong organizational and project management skills. title: Sr. Technical Dealer Support Specialist
jd_text: Senior Technical Dealer Support Specialist Why Mobility Global? As we shape the next generation of automotive intelligence through innovation, AI, and industry-leading data, we're creating new opportunities for our customers, our business, and our people. Founded in 2012, automotiveMastermind, a part of Mobility Global, is the automotive industry's trusted data and technology provider. The company drives greater salesperson efficiency through its use of Actionable Intelligence and personalized experience. Through a combination of behavioral predictive analytics, targeted marketing outreach, and expert consulting, automotiveMastermind empowers dealers and OEMs to seamlessly blend data and intelligence with personalized insights. Our Company was founded on the idea that there are patterns in people’s behavior that, with the right logic, can be used to predict future outcomes. We are a small but rapidly growing organization that works in partnership with our customers to create solutions that are simply not found anywhere else. We work in groups rather than in structured corporate hierarchies; our culture is creative and entrepreneurial where everyone contributes to company goals in very real way. We are a hardworking group, but we have a lot of fun with what we do and are looking for new people with a similar mindset to join the organization. Our proprietary software-as-a-service helps automotive dealerships and sales teams better understand and predict exactly which customers are ready to buy, the reasons why, and the key offers and incentives most likely to close the sale. Its micro-marketing engine then delivers the right message at the right time to those customers, ensuring higher conversion rates and a stronger ROI . What You'll Do • Serve as a subject matter expert on automotiveMastermind products, systems, processes, and initiatives while providing exceptional support to internal and external customers. • Resolve complex technical issues escalated from Level 1 by troubleshooting, investigating root causes, prioritizing incidents, and coordinating escalations to other support teams as needed. • Manage inbound inquiries from Business Partners and Field Teams, documenting troubleshooting efforts, setting stakeholder expectations, and providing updates through Slack, email, text, and video conferencing. • Create and maintain knowledge resources, including Knowledge Base articles, FAQs, best practices, system documentation, and training materials to improve team effectiveness and customer self-service. • Coach, mentor, and train Level 1 team members on troubleshooting best practices, product releases, new initiatives, and overall support readiness. • Administer and optimize the Zendesk environment, including user management, reporting and dashboards, workflow automations, macros, web forms, process improvements, and participation in recruiting and interviewing new team members. title: Senior Manager, Data Engineering
jd_text: 7-Eleven is an iconic family of brands with over 86,000 locations, surpassing every retailer in the world. We revolutionize convenience, restaurants and fuel through cutting edge innovation — working hard to be the customer's first choice. 7-Eleven empowers our employees to "activate awesome" and make a meaningful impact in their stores and communities every day. If you're ready to grow, lead and make a difference, come join our team and help shape the future of convenience. We are looking for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead the Data Engineering team. At 7-Eleven, Enterprise Data powers decisions for everyone from store managers to the C-suite. The Data Engineering team is the backbone of that ecosystem — designing and operating the batch and streaming ELT pipelines, lakehouse models, and master data systems that feed hundreds of enterprise reports, daily decision reports, and downstream AI applications You will lead a multi-pod team responsible for ingestion, transformation, modeling, and run-engineering across nine business domains. Responsibilities As the Senior Manager of the Data Engineering team, you will: · Manage day-to-day delivery across multiple Data Engineering pods (~25–30 engineers across onshore/offshore teams), building and operating ingestion, ELT, streaming, and lakehouse pipelines across business domains such as Digital, Merchandising, Operations, Finance, Customer & Marketing, Fuel, and Supply Chain. · Set the technical vision for Data Engineering—driving enterprise master data programs, historical/backfill strategy, intake maturity, change-control automation, and modernization of legacy ETL into a lakehouse architecture. · Partner with Data Architects to translate conceptual and logical models into physical implementations using Delta/Lakehouse platforms—applying medallion patterns, dimensional modeling, and consistent intake contracts. · Partner with Data Platform, Governance, and Quality teams to ensure every pipeline includes observability, data quality rules, lineage, and privacy classifications by design. · Own delivery of legacy reporting and analytics modernization initiatives—refactoring OLAP-style models into dimensional models, repointing reports to modern BI platforms, and decommissioning legacy systems. · Run the Data Engineering function as a product organization—managing backlog, business cases, enterprise prioritization, and adoption/value tracking for delivered data products. · Mentor engineers, technical leads, and managers, and coach offshore engineering teams on modernization, code quality, and developer experience standards. · Partner with Platform teams on CI/CD, AI-assisted SDLC, and cost attribution to ensure data workloads are observable, attributable, and cost-efficient. · Own incident response and SLA adherence for production pipelines supporting critical business and AI-driven applications. Qualifications · 8+ years of professional experience in Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or Analytics Engineering. · 5+ years designing and operating large-scale data pipelines (batch and streaming ELT/ETL) in lakehouse or data warehouse environments. · 5+ years working with distributed compute frameworks (Spark/Databricks strongly preferred; Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Workflows, DLT a plus). · 5+ years managing engineering teams, ideally across multiple pods with hybrid onshore/offshore delivery models. · Strong knowledge of data modeling (dimensional/Kimball, data vault, medallion patterns) and experience translating conceptual models into physical implementations. · Strong knowledge of master data management concepts and reference data governance. · Strong knowledge of cloud data platforms (Azure preferred; AWS or GCP acceptable). · Experience with data quality, observability, and lineage tooling, and embedding these into pipeline development. · Experience operating production data pipelines, including SLAs, on-call, incident management, and Tier 2/3 support in collaboration with platform/SRE teams. · Familiarity with AI/ML data pipelines, including feature engineering and ML-Ops handoffs. · Strong communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to present technical concepts and progress to executive and business stakeholders. · Strong project management discipline, including roadmaps, process documentation, and executive status reporting. #LI-PP1 If an hourly or salary range is included in this ad it represents the range 7-Eleven in good faith believes is the range of compensation for this role at the time of this posting. title: Lead Workforce Intelligence Consultant
jd_text: McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care. What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you. Overview People Analytics at McKesson sits at the intersection of business strategy, workforce intelligence, and executive decision-making. As part of McKesson’s HR organization, the People Analytics team partners with senior HR and business leaders to translate workforce data into decision-ready insights that shape strategy, guide action, and enable measurable business outcomes. McKesson is a diversified healthcare company that touches virtually every aspect of the industry, spanning pharmaceutical distribution, oncology and multispecialty care, prescription technology solutions, and medical-surgical supply and logistics. Across these businesses, McKesson partners with pharmaceutical manufacturers, pharmacies, providers, health plans, and government stakeholders to help ensure medicines and therapies reach the patients who need them—safely, reliably, and affordably—while investing in innovation, digital tools, and AI to keep healthcare moving. The Lead Workforce Intelligence Consultant will serve as the strategic analytics and advisory partner to HR's Leadership Team, translating workforce priorities into executive-ready data and insights that inform strategic decisions, drive measurable outcomes, and shape how HR leadership engages with workforce data. In this role, you will connect business strategy to People Analytics by shaping demand, framing the right business questions with stakeholders, prioritizing the highest-impact work, and delivering decision-ready analyses that guide action and enable outcomes related to business performance, organizational health, and growth. You will apply a wide range of analytical tools and techniques to create data-driven narratives and presentations, supporting programs, events, and leadership forums. title: Product Manager, Economy
jd_text: SciPlay is a leading developer and publisher of digital games on mobile and web platforms, providing highly entertaining free-to-play games that millions of people play every day for their authenticity, engagement and fun. SciPlay currently offers nine core games, including social casino games Jackpot Party Casino, Gold Fish Casino Slots, Hot Shot Casino and Quick Hit Slots, and casual games MONOPOLY Slots, Bingo Showdown, 88 Fortunes Slots, Backgammon Live and Solitaire Pet Adventure with offices all over the world! Position Summary We're hiring a Product Manager, Economy to be the economic brain behind our games. You will specialize in tuning the economy (what things cost, what they give, and how fast players progress) and you will share LiveOps, monitoring and monetization with the teams that run them day to day. If you like modeling incentives and then watching real players prove you right or wrong, this is the job. The economist's mindset Thinks in incentives: what a change makes players do, not only what it costs or earns. Reads an economy as flows: sources, sinks, inflation, and the marginal effect of each tweak. Trades short-term revenue against long-term economy health, and says which one a decision favors. Decides from data, models and experiments rather than intuition, then writes the reasoning down. What you will own Own the design of the game economy: currencies, sources and sinks, progression, and the pricing of virtual goods, with clear KPIs that show whether it is healthy. Tune the economy week to week: feature configurations, rewards, level progression, bonus values and offer contents, using data and experiments to fine-tune. Build simulations and predictive models that forecast how content, pricing and balance changes will land before they ship. Plan, run and read A/B tests on economy and pricing changes, and turn the results into decisions. Define player segments from behavior and motivation, and tailor economy parameters to each segment. Own monitoring of economy health (player balances, inflation, source and sink ratios, conversion) and act on anomalies. Partner with Product, Design, Analytics, Marketing and Engineering so the economy supports game goals, and present recommendations to senior leadership. What you will share Co-owned with LiveOps, Monetization and Analytics Partner with Monetization on offers, bundles and price points. You own the economic guardrails (value per dollar, inflation, effect on progression); Monetization owns offer execution and revenue targets. Co-own LiveOps with the LiveOps team: you define the economy of each event (costs, rewards, pacing); LiveOps owns scheduling, configuration and QA. Help Product and Monetization make the experience-versus-revenue trade-off explicit. What we are looking for Ownership mindset; comfortable with ambiguity and switching context quickly. Nice to have Degree in economics, mathematics, statistics, engineering or another quantitative field. 3+ years in game economy, F2P product management or a closely related analytical role. Advanced spreadsheet modeling (Excel or Sheets) for balance models and simulations. Working knowledge of statistics and probability, and of simulation methods such as Monte Carlo. Python or R for analysis and modeling. Hands-on experience designing and reading A/B tests. Understanding of behavioral economics and player motivation. Background in mobile, online or social free-to-play games. Familiarity with LiveOps tooling and event operations, and a habit of working alongside a LiveOps team. Clear communicator who turns models into recommendations that stakeholders at every level can act on. Genuine passion for games, and a habit of playing the genre. We are SciPlay! We make games! At SciPlay, we are programmed to think untraditionally, and we believe in doing what you love and doing it well. We take pride in our ability to stay ahead of the game! We are the brainiacs behind-the-scenes; innovating, dreaming, and navigating the social gaming world. title: Sales Floor Dept Supervisor - Building Materials
jd_text: What You Will Do All Lowe’s associates deliver quality customer service while maintaining a store that is clean, safe, and stocked with the products our customers need. The Sales Floor Department Supervisor is primarily responsible for leading and enabling a team of associates to deliver the best possible customer experience in the store. This includes coaching and training associates, delegating, following-up on daily tasks, managing performance, and ensuring adequate department coverage. Sales Floor Department Supervisors are responsible for customer-facing activities (e.g., greeting customers, clarifying needs and identifying solutions, closing sales), non-customer-facing activities (e.g., down stocking, inventory management, area recovery) and store safety (e.g., conducting safety walks, reporting hazards, understanding safety and lifting directions). Further, the Sales Floor Department Supervisor must supervise associates in other departments, as needed, to meet the demands of the store. This requires broad product knowledge and the ability to engage associates and customers across departments. In addition to the responsibilities summarized above, individuals in this role may occasionally open or close the store or serve as manager-on-duty (MOD). title: Technical Project Manager, Data
jd_text: It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing! We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business. LucyRx is seeking a Technical Project Manager to bring structure, clarity, and momentum to our data engineering organization. As we modernize our data platform, migrate legacy Oracle systems to the cloud, and build out Snowflake-based analytics infrastructure, the volume and complexity of incoming work is growing. This role exists to make sure that work flows smoothly: from intake and requirements through scoping, prioritization, execution, and delivery. You will be the connective tissue between business stakeholders who need data and the engineers who build it. You understand enough about data and technology to ask the right questions, push back on vague requirements, and protect the team from scope creep. You are comfortable running a standup, managing a backlog, and having a direct conversation when something is off track. You do not need to write code, but you need to understand what the engineers are building and why it matters. Maintain a clear, prioritized view of incoming requests and help leadership make informed tradeoff decisions. Scoping and Estimation Facilitate scoping and estimation sessions with engineering leads. Ensure work is broken down to a level of detail that allows for reliable delivery commitments. Identify dependencies, risks, and assumptions early and surface them before work begins rather than after it derails. Maintain realistic delivery timelines that account for team capacity, complexity, and competing priorities. Delivery and Execution Own the day-to-day delivery cadence for active data engineering work. Run standups, facilitate sprint planning and retrospectives, and keep the team moving. Track progress against commitments and identify variance early. Escalate when something is at risk and propose solutions rather than just problems. Remove blockers. Whether it is a missing access credential, an unclear requirement, or a dependency on another team, you clear the path so engineers can focus on building. Maintain accurate and up-to-date project documentation including status reports, decision logs, and delivery timelines. Prioritization and Backlog Management Maintain and groom the data engineering backlog in collaboration with the Manager, Data Engineering and other stakeholders. Facilitate prioritization conversations that balance business urgency, technical dependencies, team capacity, and strategic roadmap alignment. Ensure the team always knows what they are working on, why it matters, and what comes next. Stakeholder Communication Serve as the primary point of contact for stakeholders seeking status on data engineering work. Provide proactive, clear, and honest updates. Set and manage expectations on delivery timelines. Do not over-promise and do not go silent when something slips. Build strong working relationships across the data, engineering, product, clinical, and finance teams. Prepare and present project status updates for leadership as needed. Qualifications and Education Requirements Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 5+ years of project management experience, with at least 3 years managing technical data or engineering projects. Demonstrated experience working with data engineering, analytics, or BI teams in a project management capacity. Strong understanding of data concepts: pipelines, ETL/ELT, data warehousing, and reporting workflows. You do not need to build these things, but you need to understand them well enough to scope and manage them. Proficiency with Agile, Scrum, or Kanban delivery frameworks. Comfortable running ceremonies, managing sprints, and adapting process to what the team actually needs. Experience with project and backlog management tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Confluence, or similar. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. You can write a crisp status update, run a focused meeting, and have a direct conversation when something is off track. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. You keep things from falling through the cracks. Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment where processes are still being built. Preferences Experience managing projects involving Oracle databases, cloud data platforms (Snowflake, AWS, Azure), or data migration initiatives. Familiarity with modern data stack tools such as dbt, Fivetran, Airflow, or Tableau. Healthcare, PBM, managed care, or other regulated industry experience. PMP, PMI-ACP, CSM, or equivalent certification. Experience working with mixed teams of FTE and contractors. Exposure to HIPAA compliance requirements in a technical project context. Position Summary The Director, Customer Facing Demand Planning sits within the demand planning organization, part of the Supply Chain Inventory Planning team and serves as the primary owner of customer– level demand execution for a n assigned segment . This role leads a team of ~10 FTE and reports to the Sr. Director of Customer Facing Demand Planning . They execute the customer-specific demand remit for the assigned segment, managing inventory position ing, and service levels at the account level, while capturing and qualifying inbound demand signals including new product launches, and translating that customer intelligence back into the consensus planning process . Key Responsibilities Customer Demand Execution Manage the day-to-day customer-facing demand function for the assigned segment , ensuring the team executes against established standards a s a high-responsiveness partner to customers and cross-functional stakeholders. Maintain the sequestration and strategic customer program model for the assigned segment, ensuring inventory is accurately bucketed, program commitments are honored, and customers have reliable access to the inventory they are entitled to; oversee customer portfolio management including formulary changes, product switches, and customer-specific inventory positions. Direct the customer onboarding function for new accounts, ensuring inventory builds, allocation planning, and system setup are executed in a coordinated, go-live ready manner. Manage escalations and serve as the primary point of escalation for customer facing communication within the assigned segment , resolving service level inquiries, and ensuring contractual requirements are tracked and met, escalating to the Sr. Director when required . Ensure customer-specific award switch execution is completed accurately and on time for the assigned accounts. Demand Signal Intake & Translation Execute the demand signal intake process for the assigned segment , ensuring the team captures, validates , and enriches customer intelligence against established quality standards before passing inputs to the consensus demand planning team. Monitor and manage upstream demand inputs for the assigned segment , including program changes, new launch items, promotional activity, and customer specific shifts ensuring they are ca ptured proactively and reflected in the plan before they create a supply risk. Maintain an active working relationship with the consensus demand planning team, ensuring demand signal inputs are understood, accepted, and incorporated into the consensus forecast without delays or misalignment. Service Level Reporting & Analytics Manage service level performance for assigned segment , e nsuring the team produces accurate , timely service level reports and national tracking metrics that enable proactive management of service risk. Conduct and direct root cause analysis on service level escalations and omits for assigned accounts, holding the team accountable to identifying precipitating events and driving remediation. Maintain and improve analytical capability within the team, including dashboards, data queries, and reporting tools that surface allocation and policy decisions faster and with greater accuracy. Team Leadership, Development & Continuous Improvement Manage and develop a customer-facing demand team for assigned segment , holding team members accountable to performance expectations, role clarity, and the operating standards set by the Sr. Director. Coach and develop team members toward greater ownership and capability, providing regular feedback, identifying development opportunities, and creating visibility into advancement paths within the demand planning organization. Partner with the other Directors of Customer Facing Demand to drive continuous improvement efforts, share leading practice s and drive consistency across teams. Maintain a close pulse on team workload, capacity, and execution quality across accounts , proactively identifying resource constraints or process gaps before they affect customer service or demand signal accura cy. Minimum Requirement Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience. Education Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain , Business or related field, or equivalent experience. Critical Skills 1 2 + years in supply chain, demand planning, or customer operations roles with at least 4 years in a leadership capacity managing teams and driving cross functional outcomes. Elevating the quality and reliability of the demand signal entering the consensus planning process through disciplined intake governance and rigorous enrichment practices. Building trusted relationships with customers and cross– functional partners while maintaining the objectivity required to make hard calls on the forecast. Managing a high volume, operationally intensive account portfolio with precision. Functional proficiency in Kinaxis Maestro or comparable advanced planning system. Demonstrated experience leading customer-facing teams in a complex, high-volume distribution, p harmaceutical environment, with direct accountability for service levels. Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills. Proven ability to influence without direct authority across a matrixed organization. Additional Skills St rong communication sk ills - ability to re present the segment credibly in leadership forums and translate operational complexity into clear strategic framing. Experience managing sequestration programs, or high-touch strategic customer inventory models. Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally across demand planning, supply planning, and inventory management teams. Demonstrated ability to balance customer advocacy with the analytical discipline required to challenge demand signals that do not reflect system or market reality. Familiar with demand planning analytics and reporting tools, including dashboards and data queries that support account-level service level management. Physical Requirements Traditional office requirements. A large percentage of time performing computer-based work is required. Hybrid role, must live near Las Colinas office. Up to 25% travel. Title: Sr. Director, Enterprise Compliance Effectiveness & Experience Location: Dallas, TX (REQUIRED) Onsite / Remote / Hybrid: Hybrid As part of the Enterprise Compliance Programs team, the Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance Effectiveness & Experience (“Senior Director”) is responsible for strengthening the effectiveness, maturity, and stakeholder experience of McKesson’s Enterprise Compliance Program. The role leads McKesson’s structured, year-over-year Compliance Program effectiveness assessment framework, providing an evidence-based view of program maturity, identifying improvement priorities, guiding remediation, and supporting credible engagement with regulators and other external stakeholders. The Senior Director also leads key components of the Compliance function’s modernization. This includes translating the Enterprise Compliance technology strategy into a multi-year roadmap and leading the business transformation, process design, adoption, and value realization associated with McKesson’s evolving Compliance technology ecosystem. The role aligns Enterprise and Business Unit Compliance teams around scalable, technology-enabled processes and modern ways of working. In addition, the Senior Director establishes and leads McKesson’s Enterprise Compliance Experience capability, shaping how Team McKesson accesses and engages with Compliance, how Compliance professionals perform their work and drive value across the enterprise, and how corporate functions and executive leaders’ partner with Compliance to advance organizational strategy. The role oversees the evolution of Compliance’s enterprise “front door,” including centralized monitoring of inquiries, concerns, requests for guidance, and other stakeholder contacts. The Senior Director also provides strategic compliance support to designated corporate functions and their executive leadership teams. This includes serving as an additional Speak Up channel, providing insights and reporting related to compliance culture, supporting Compliance Council meetings, and helping leaders integrate compliance considerations into organizational priorities and decision-making. This role influences senior leaders and partners across Enterprise and Business Unit Compliance, Technology, Legal, Human Resources, corporate functions, business teams, and external providers to simplify engagement, strengthen organizational trust, and build a Compliance function equipped for the future. The Senior Director reports directly to McKesson’s Vice President, Enterprise Compliance (“VP”) within McKesson’s General Counsel Organization. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience leading compliance program effectiveness, enterprise transformation, technology enablement, process modernization, stakeholder experience, and executive-facing compliance initiatives within healthcare, healthcare technology, pharmaceutical, life sciences, or similarly regulated organization. This individual must possess executive presence, regulatory credibility, strong business acumen, and the ability to influence senior leaders and drive sustained change across a highly matrixed enterprise. A demonstrated commitment to McKesson’s LEAD Rx behaviors, continuous improvement, innovation, collaboration, and people development is essential. Key Responsibilities A Compliance Program Effectiveness Trailblazer Leads McKesson’s enterprise framework for evaluating, demonstrating, and continuously improving the effectiveness and maturity of the Compliance Program. Defines and executes McKesson's enterprise Compliance Program assessment framework, leveraging regulatory expectations, external developments, and leading practices. Leads assessments of program design, implementation, effectiveness, and maturity across enterprise and business unit activities. Establishes defensible methodologies, evidence standards, reporting, and improvement plans that provide leaders with clear visibility into program strengths, gaps, and priorities. Provides leadership with a longitudinal view of program maturity, remediation progress, and the effectiveness of Compliance investments. A Technology Transformation Strategist Leads the business transformation, adoption, and value realization required to modernize Compliance through technology. Translates the Enterprise Compliance technology strategy into a multi-year roadmap of prioritized capabilities, investments, and transformation initiatives aligned with evolving regulatory, business, program, and stakeholder needs. Leads business transformation, adoption, and value realization associated with GRC platforms and other strategic Compliance technologies. Identifies and prioritizes automation, analytics, AI, and emerging technology opportunities that improve effectiveness, efficiency, scalability, and engagement. Provides executive visibility into transformation progress, adoption, dependencies, risks, and realized value. A Strategic Technology and Supplier Relationship Leader Establish the governance and strategic relationships required to sustain McKesson’s Compliance technology ecosystem and long-term transformation objectives. Serves as the senior Compliance relationship owner for strategic technology providers, aligning vendor roadmaps, performance, platform capabilities, contractual commitments, and investment decisions with enterprise priorities. Partners with Technology, Legal, Procurement, Information Security, business stakeholders, and external providers to establish clear governance, decision rights, escalation pathways, and accountability. Ensures Compliance technology solutions continue to evolve with regulatory requirements, business priorities, stakeholder needs, and Compliance Program objectives. Promotes scalable enterprise capabilities and reduces unnecessary duplication or fragmentation across Compliance technology solutions. An Enterprise Compliance Experience Architect Establishes and leads the enterprise capability for designing how Team McKesson engages with Compliance and how Compliance professionals perform their work. Defines and executes the enterprise strategy for how employees, leaders, and Compliance professionals engage with Compliance. Leads the evolution of Compliance's enterprise "front door," including participation in the Unified Service Agent environment and oversight of intake, routing, service standards, and stakeholder communications. The role leads a team of three direct reports and one indirect report, establishes clear priorities and review standards, and remains directly engaged in complex analyses, executive materials, governance decisions, and issue resolution. Success requires strong executive communication, disciplined financial stewardship, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to improve processes through standardization, automation, and scalable reporting. Key Responsibilities Strategic FP&A Leadership and Business Partnership Own the financial agenda for all HQ and IT operating expense, aligning resources and investments with Practice Management, US Oncology, and enterprise priorities. Advise senior leaders on financial performance, choices, risks, opportunities, trade-offs, and recommended actions; translate complex cost and allocation topics into decision-ready insights. Lead cross-functional work across Finance, Accounting, Technology, Strategy, Operations, Ontada, McKesson Technology, and other business units to resolve issues and advance shared objectives. Develop recommendations that clarify service scope, funding mechanisms, practice cost sharing, pricing or service-fee considerations, and the financial impact of allocation changes. Challenge new and existing spend, identify savings and cost-avoidance opportunities, and facilitate prioritization and trade-off decisions within financial targets. Build durable processes for gross-to-net expense visibility, headcount and cost-center mapping, decision logs, and ongoing tracking of allocation outcomes. Technology Finance and Investment Decision Support Lead planning, forecasting, and reporting for US Oncology technology costs, including retained and practice-allocated expense, enterprise technology allocations, subscriptions, infrastructure, and strategic programs. Foster an inclusive, collaborative, accountable culture that encourages thoughtful challenge, continuous learning, and sustainable ways of working. Education Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent related experience. MBA, CPA, CMA, or other relevant advanced credential preferred. Critical Skills Typically 12+ years of progressive finance, FP&A, accounting, or related analytical experience, including 4+ years of management responsibility. Demonstrated experience leading planning, forecasting, close analysis, management reporting, financial modeling, and executive decision support in a complex organization. title: Director, Accounting - Nashville, TN
jd_text: It’s More Than a Career, It’s a Mission. Our people are the foundation of our success. By joining our growing team at Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI), a subsidiary of McKesson, you will have the opportunity to become part of one of the largest community-based cancer programs to advance oncology treatments and improve outcomes for cancer patients across the globe. We look for mission-driven candidates who have a desire to advance the fight against cancer and make a difference in the lives of patients diagnosed with cancer every day. Our Mission People who live with cancer – those who work to prevent it, fight it, and survive it – are at the heart of every decision we make. Bringing the most innovative medical minds together with the most passionate caregivers in their communities, we are transforming care and personalizing treatment. Through clinical excellence and cutting-edge research, SCRI is redefining cancer care around the world. The Director, Accounting serves all Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) lines of business and is responsible for leading accounting operations, financial reporting, month-end close, balance sheet integrity, accounts payable oversight, and the internal control environment. This position ensures financial information is accurate, timely, and compliant with U.S. GAAP, company policies, and applicable regulatory requirements. This is a hybrid position based at our Nashville, TN corporate offices. Relocation assistance and visa sponsorship are not available. The Director, Accounting partners closely with Revenue Cycle, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Operations, Legal, Tax, Treasury, Technical Accounting, Information Technology, Internal Audit, and external auditors. The role supports organizational growth, system integrations, mergers and other new business operations, while driving process improvement, automation, staff development, and standardization across SCRI accounting functions. Duties include and are not limited to: Financial Reporting and Close Process Lead and oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close activities. Accounting Operations and Governance Oversee general ledger accounting activities across SCRI lines of business. Revenue Recognition Governance Partner with Technical Accounting, Revenue Cycle, and operational leadership to evaluate complex accounting transactions, contract modifications, revenue recognition matters, and new business arrangements. Balance Sheet Integrity and Reconciliations Ensure timely preparation and review of balance sheet reconciliations. Accounts Payable Oversight Provide leadership and oversight of accounts payable operations. Internal Controls, Compliance, and Audit Support Maintain an effective financial control environment. Systems, Integrations, and New Business Operations Provide accounting leadership for financial system implementations, upgrades, interfaces, and integrations. Strategic Initiatives and Process Improvement Lead automation, standardization, and continuous improvement initiatives across Accounting. Partner with Revenue Cycle, FP&A, Information Technology, and Finance leadership to improve workflows and data quality. Leadership and Talent Development Recruit, develop, coach, and retain a high-performing accounting team. Executive and Governance Support Prepare materials, analyses, and presentations supporting executive leadership, audit activities, financial statement reviews, and other governance-related reporting requirements. Qualifications for success include: Bachelor Degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field required. Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license required Eight or more years of progressive accounting experience. Five or more years of people leadership experience. Demonstrated experience leading month-end close, financial reporting, accounting operations, and internal controls. Healthcare, clinical research, life sciences, or multi-entity accounting experience preferred. Experience supporting acquisitions, purchase accounting, post-close integration, or similar transaction accounting activities preferred. Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, financial reporting requirements, and accounting policy application. Thorough understanding of internal controls, accounting governance, and audit support. Experience with ERP systems, financial reporting tools, system integrations, and process automation. About Sarah Cannon Research Institute Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) is one of the world’s leading oncology research organizations conducting community-based clinical trials. Focused on advancing therapies for patients over the last three decades, SCRI is a leader in drug development. In 2022, SCRI formed a joint venture with former US Oncology Research to expand clinical trial access across the country. It has conducted more than 850 first-in-human clinical trials since its inception and contributed to pivotal research that has led to the majority of new cancer therapies approved by the FDA in the past decade. title: Senior Director, Revenue Cycle Finance
jd_text: McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care. What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you. USON Overview The US Oncology Network is a leader in community-based oncology care, bringing together independent oncology providers to deliver connected care in local communities. The Network manages practice business operations, including billing, non-medical personnel, facilities management, technology, and payer contracting, enabling practices to remain independent while benefiting from shared expertise, coordinated resources, and the support of McKesson. By enhancing operational efficiency and providing tools that support practice growth and innovation, The Network enables providers to focus on what matters most: their patients. Role Overview The Senior Director, Revenue Cycle Management Finance is the senior finance leader for The US Oncology Network’s Revenue Cycle Management organization and a member of the US Oncology Network FP&A leadership team. The role leads Revenue Cycle Management FP&A, Revenue Accounting, and a newly established Balance Sheet Reconciliations function through three Director-level leaders. This leader integrates planning, revenue accounting, controllership, working capital, transformation finance, analytics, and practice support to improve financial outcomes and confidence in reported results. Key Responsibilities Revenue Cycle Financial Strategy, Performance & Executive Partnership Lead planning, forecasting, long-range outlooks, performance reporting, and executive decision support for Revenue Cycle Management. Connect operational drivers to cash, expense, bad debt, and Adjusted Operating Profit outcomes and recommend actions to senior leaders. Build a standing, network-wide partnership model across Operations, practices, Finance, Accounting, and Controllership. Working Capital, Cash Flow & Accounts Receivable Stewardship Lead analysis of cash collections, accounts receivable aging, collectability, denials, bad debt, reserve exposure, and recovery performance. Guide cash forecasting and scenario modeling, including aging transitions, practice impacts, and recovery plans following disruption. Establish performance measures and escalation routines for working capital and revenue-cycle outcomes. Revenue Accounting, iReserve & Reporting Governance Provide strategic oversight of Revenue Accounting, including iReserve, contractual discount methodologies, reserve analytics, revenue recognition support, monthly close, and reporting. Resolve complex revenue and reserve matters with Accounting and Controllership and strengthen assumption governance and transparency. Oversee Revenue Cycle SOX controls, documentation, remediation, and audit readiness. Balance Sheet Reconciliations Function Build & Management Stand up and manage a new Director-led Balance Sheet Reconciliations function to centralize and strengthen accounts receivable and cash-clearing reconciliations. Define service scope, staffing, standard work, documentation, quality criteria, governance, escalation protocols, and performance metrics. Drive resolution of reconciling items, aged balances, ownership gaps, and control deficiencies while expanding Controller support. Transformation, Technology & Value Realization Lead finance support for operating-model redesign, technology modernization, billing-system transitions, automation, and AI-enabled workflow initiatives. Develop business cases, value-driver models, implementation economics, and benefits tracking from concept through sustained performance. Translate financial targets into executable plans and transparent outcome reporting with Operations and Technology. Data, Analytics & Scalable Reporting Advance analytics, data governance, modeling, reporting, and decision-support capabilities across the Network. Standardize and automate recurring analyses, improve data quality and traceability, and create scalable self-service capabilities. Communicate decision-oriented insights, forward-looking risks, and required actions. Organizational Leadership, Talent & Business Continuity Lead, coach, and develop three Director-level leaders and their teams with clear accountability and succession plans. Build an inclusive, high-performing organization across FP&A, accounting, controllership, analytics, and transformation. Lead scenario analysis and executive support during operational disruptions, system outages, and critical enterprise issues. General Responsibilities Cultivate a diverse and inclusive culture that encourages thoughtful challenge and healthy debate. Build strong relationships across Operations, practices, Finance, Accounting, Controllership, Technology, Compliance, and Internal Audit. Develop high-performing teams while role-modeling I²CARE and LEADRx behaviors. Drive operational maturity through standardization, automation, AI-enabled capabilities, and enterprise solutions. Deliver accurate, timely, well-controlled work in a high-pressure environment. jd_text: We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 19 Oct 2026 Careers that change lives start here. Our industry-leading portfolio of transcatheter valve therapies and enabling technologies is redefining how clinicians treat aortic, congenital, mitral, and tricuspid valve disease. Together, we're helping expand access to innovative treatments, improving procedural outcomes, and delivering meaningful impact for patients living with complex heart conditions. title: Director, Implementation Services, Enterprise
jd_text: Join the Team Modernizing Medicine At ModMed , we’re not just building software—we’re reimagining the healthcare experience. Founded in 2010 by a practicing physician and a successful tech entrepreneur, we took a radically different approach: we hired doctors and taught them how to code. This "for doctors, by doctors" philosophy has allowed us to create an AI-enabled, specialty-specific cloud platform that places patients at the center of care. A Culture of Excellence When you join ModMed, you’re joining an award-winning team recognized for innovation and employee satisfaction. From our global headquarters in Boca Raton Florida, and extensive employee base in Hyderabad India, we are a team of 4,500+ passionate problem-solvers on a mission to increase medical practice success and improve patient outcomes: Consistently ranked as a Top Place to Work 2025 Globee Business Awards: Gold Globee for “Technology Team of the Year” 2025 Black Book Awards: Ranked #1 EHR in 11 Specialties Florida Venture Forum: Venture-Backed Company of the Year We are growing fast, thinking big, and we are just getting started. Ready to modernize medicine with us? Job Description Summary: The Director, Professional Services will be responsible for the design, implementation and management of various Professional Services organizations (Enterprise Project Management, Business Consulting, Pay Implementations) and personnel per strategic departmental KPI requirements. In alignment with our company culture, the Director will be guided by our core values: be agile, pursue effectiveness and efficiency, earn trust, and champion innovation. This role will work closely with Sales Organization, Training Services, Technology Services, and Operations teams to develop processes to meet and exceed our clients’ expectations. Job Responsibilities: Leads Professional Services teams who oversee the implementation and execution of tasks associated with the full suite of ModMed products, solutions, and integrations. Takes ownership of team successes by directing, mentoring, and coaching. Manifests an understanding of project management practices and principles (constraints, risks/issues management, best practices, etc.) Serves as an escalation point for issues beyond team authority; resolves conflicts involving project priorities, resources, and/or contractual issues with the client. Demonstrates the ability to quickly understand a business situation; make prompt decisions to facilitate the expedition of resolutions and navigate to successful outcomes. Builds positive working relationships/partnerships and a trusted advisor within the organization, consulting practice managers, clients, and is recognized by the client as the delivery executive responsible for the ensuring overall delivery experience. Ensures adherence to quality standards and documented processes in day-to-day activities. Interfaces with client project stakeholders, including C-level management and directors, to elicit business and functional requirements. Proactively addresses performance concerns with the applicable manager; provides performance evaluation input for project resources. Has a thorough understanding of the business's key performance indicators and metrics and manages them to successful levels consistently. Proactively manages the financial details of the business, including but not limited to forecasting revenue, concessions/credits, backlog management, and EBITDA. Works collaboratively with the leadership team to develop and/or improve the practice as a whole, including strategies, policies, and processes; supports and promotes the use of leading-edge delivery methodologies and best practices. Job Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Healthcare Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. Demonstrated leadership abilities to effectively lead a cross-functional client-driven organization. 5+ years of Electronic Health Record implementations leadership experience. 5+ years of experience leading Practice Management/Revenue Cycle Management implementations. Ability to quickly learn, analyze, understand, and convey complex information. Excellent verbal and written communication and listening skills. Ability to effectively work independently and coordinate team efforts. Experience with Salesforce or related implementation and CRM software solutions. Quality Assurance management Expert knowledge of creating and managing a Project Management organization. Generous Paid Time Off and Paid Parental Leave programs, Company paid Life and Disability benefits, Flexible Spending Account, and Employee Assistance Programs, Company-sponsored Business Resource & Special Interest Groups that provide engaged and supportive communities within ModMed, Professional development opportunities, including tuition reimbursement programs and unlimited access to LinkedIn Learning , Global presence and in-person collaboration opportunities; dog-friendly HQ (US), Hybrid office-based roles and remote availability for some roles, Weekly catered breakfast and lunch, treadmill workstations, Zen, and wellness rooms within our BRIC headquarters. title: Platform Architect
jd_text: Are you passionate about making a difference in people's lives? Do you enjoy working in a service-oriented industry? If so, this opportunity may be the right fit for you! Modivcare is looking for an experienced Platform Architect to join our team. As a Cloud Platform Architect, you will serve as a senior, hands-on technical leader within our Architecture practice, bringing deep cloud-native expertise, delivery involvement, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) discipline. You will define cloud architecture, build and validate infrastructure using Pulumi or AWS CDK, and work alongside engineering teams throughout delivery to ensure what is built matches what was designed. Your work will directly impact the scalability, security, cost efficiency, and reliability of the technology platforms that support Modivcare’ s business and the services we provide. This role offers the opportunity to shape our cloud capabilities while enabling engineering teams to deliver solutions that make a meaningful difference for the people and communities we serve. We’re looking for purpose-driven applicants who are motivated by using technology to solve meaningful business challenges, improve how teams deliver critical services, and build sustainable solutions that support Modivcare’ s mission. The ideal candidate combines strategic architecture expertise with a willingness to remain hands-on throughout delivery and takes ownership of turning well-designed architecture into measurable business impact. This role… Architecture & Design Defines cloud-native architecture patterns for the enterprise, covering compute, networking, storage, security, identity, and AI/ML workload infrastructure on AWS. Establishes and evolves cloud architecture standards, guardrails, and reference architectures that enable engineering teams to build secure, scalable, and consistent solutions. Evaluates new AWS services, IaC patterns, and platform capabilities, making build vs. buy vs. configure decisions with clear rationale and consideration for business value. Designs multi-account AWS organization structures, landing zones, and network topologies appropriate to healthcare compliance requirements, including HIPAA and SOC 2. Architects cost-efficient, right-sized infrastructure with FinOps principles embedded into the design from the start. Hands-On Delivery Builds and maintains infrastructure-as-code using Pulumi (TypeScript/Python) as the primary tool, with AWS CDK considered where Pulumi is not the right fit. Prototypes cloud infrastructure for new initiatives end-to-end, proving the architecture works before handing it off to engineering teams to scale and operate. Contributes directly to IaC repositories, writing production-quality Pulumi stacks that engineering teams can maintain, extend, and operate without rearchitecting. Works embedded with engineering teams during delivery phases, reviewing PRs, unblocking infrastructure decisions, and ensuring architectural fidelity through deployment. Produces complete handoff packages, including architecture diagrams, IaC repositories, runbooks, security and compliance documentation, and acceptance criteria. Maintains a clear boundary between architecture and operations, focusing on design quality and delivery excellence rather than incident response, on-call rotation, or day-to-day platform operations. Practice Leadership Provides technical direction to the offshore Cloud & Infrastructure Solutions Delivery Architect, reviewing architectures, setting standards, and mentoring on cloud-native delivery. Partners with the Director of Architecture on cloud strategy, roadmap, and investment decisions. Engages with business unit stakeholders to understand workload requirements and translates them into cloud architecture recommendations that support business objectives. Contributes to the broader Architecture practice by sharing patterns, leading cloud-focused guilds or working groups, and building the team’s collective cloud capability. Maintains awareness of the evolving AWS service landscape and healthcare compliance requirements, proactively surfacing relevant changes to the Architecture practice and engineering leadership. We are interested in speaking with individuals with the following… Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field required; equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. Seven (7) or more years of progressively responsible experience in cloud architecture or cloud engineering, with the majority of recent experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale AWS solutions. Demonstrated experience designing and implementing enterprise AWS cloud platforms, including multi-account strategies, cloud governance, and Infrastructure as Code. Experience developing cloud platforms within regulated industries, such as healthcare or other highly regulated environments, preferred. Experience working in embedded architecture or product delivery teams preferred. AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional and/or AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional certifications preferred. Experience with AWS CDK, AI/ML infrastructure, healthcare data platforms, and FinOps tools preferred. Expert knowledge of AWS cloud technologies, including compute (EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda), networking (VPC, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect), storage (S3, EFS, RDS, DynamoDB), and security services (IAM, KMS, Service Control Policies, GuardDuty, Security Hub). Advanced knowledge of cloud-native architecture principles, enterprise platform design, and multi-account AWS environments using AWS Organizations and Control Tower. Strong proficiency with Infrastructure as Code (IaC), including Pulumi (TypeScript or Python), AWS CDK, Git-based development workflows, modular architecture, state management, policy-as-code (e.g., Checkov, OPA), and drift detection. Demonstrated ability to design, prototype, and implement scalable, secure, and resilient cloud infrastructure solutions that align with business and technical requirements. Strong understanding of cloud governance, security, compliance, and architecture best practices, including experience supporting regulated environments such as HIPAA, SOC 2, or similar compliance frameworks. Knowledge of cloud migration strategies, cloud platform modernization, and enterprise architecture standards. Ability to evaluate emerging cloud technologies, tools, and services and recommend innovative, cost-effective solutions. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and technical decision-making skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to develop architecture documentation, technical standards, and implementation guidance for engineering, security, and business stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to provide technical leadership, mentor architects and engineers, and collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams. Ability to work independently with a high degree of autonomy while managing multiple priorities and complex technical initiatives. Preferred knowledge of AI/ML infrastructure on AWS (e.g., SageMaker, Bedrock, OpenSearch), FinOps practices and cost optimization tools, healthcare interoperability standards (e.g., HL7, FHIR, Epic), and embedded architecture delivery models. Salary: 116,700.00 – 180,000 This role is bonus eligible based on individual and company performance. The physical demands described are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. Primarily seated work; extensive computer and telephone use; occasional standing, walking, reaching, bending, and lifting up to 10 lbs. Modivcare’s positions are posted and open for applications for a minimum of 5 days. Positions may be posted for a maximum of 45 days dependent on the type of role, the number of roles, and the number of applications received. We encourage our prospective candidates to submit their application(s) expediently so as not to miss out on our opportunities. title: Lead, Inbound Destination Operations (Dallas)
jd_text: Logitech is the Sweet Spot for people who want their actions to have a positive global impact while having the flexibility to do it in their own way. Position Summary We are seeking an experienced Lead, Inbound Destination Operations based in our Dallas, TX office to oversee and drive global inbound logistics efficiency across all global Distribution Centers (DCs). While this is an individual contributor role without direct reports, high-impact leadership, ownership, and end-to-end accountability are paramount. This role carries direct responsibility for high-complexity regions, specifically 2 AMR FTZ (Foreign Trade Zone) DCs and 3 LATAM DCs, managing necessary changes in logistics operations following trade compliance policy adjustments, importation complexity, and destination container security. Working closely with our 4PL control tower teams in Asia and Mexico and 3PL partners globally, you will serve as the primary escalation point for internal and external stakeholders, building robust cross-functional trust and credibility across our end-to-end supply chain network. The ideal candidate seamlessly balances deep, hands-on operational execution in US and LATAM inbound processes with acting as a confident ambassador and representative for Logitech—balancing service quality and cost efficiency, upholding compliance and process integrity, and continuously driving operational excellence for all inbound containers into global DCs. Key Responsibilities Inbound & Control Tower Operations: Oversee inbound logistics operations into AMR FTZ DCs and LATAM DCs, ensuring strict adherence to trade compliance, importation rules, and destination container security standards. Collaborate closely with 4PL control tower teams in Asia and Mexico, serving as the primary escalation lead for internal and external stakeholders. Practical Business Analysis & Analytics: Perform hands-on, practical business analysis to translate complex logistics data into actionable operational strategies. Leverage advanced analytics using Asana, AI tools, and Power BI dashboards to evaluate network performance, maintain EDI data quality, improve ETA accuracy, and support strategic decision-making. Partner & Stakeholder Representation: Lead the comprehensive review and updating of international freight Statement of Work (SOW) documents (including Ocean, Air and all other ship modes) prior to contract reviews with Freight Forwarders (FFs). Directly represent Logitech Inbound Logistics with external suppliers, freight forwarders, 3PL/4PL partners, and DC warehouse management partners, serving as a proud and effective brand ambassador. Drive vendor performance evaluations, scorecard reviews (MBR/QBR), onboarding, SLA compliance, and service improvements. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Leadership: Partner with 4PL, 3PL, DC warehouse management, Global CSC, Trade Compliance, and Logistics Procurement to align Inbound plans, optimize service levels, and mitigate supply disruptions. Cultivate trust, influence, and peer credibility through strong execution and deep domain expertise. Risk & Exception Management: Design and enforce strict escalation and remediation processes for any operation disruptions, like critical in-transit issues, including severe delays, missing seals, theft cases, or severe cargo discrepancies requiring documentation revisions for Foreign Trade Zone (FTZ) receipts. Maintain cargo security frameworks and risk mitigation strategies across all active transportation networks. Project Execution & Process Innovation: Lead inbound supply chain optimization initiatives (network design, lead time reduction, container utilization, and landed cost control) to maximize operational efficiency and achieve cost targets. Direct logistics projects using tools like Asana to track milestones and status. Drive long-term process optimization beyond daily operational firefighting while fostering strong teamwork and fresh perspectives. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Analytics, or a related field. 8+ years of experience in global logistics or transportation management, with extensive hands-on expertise in US & LATAM inbound logistics operations, FTZ procedures, customs/trade compliance. Proven experience operating within or leading an end-to-end logistics control tower. Deep expertise and hands-on operational experience with the Global logistics market, including carrier networks, customs, and regulatory landscapes. Strong hands-on business analysis capabilities, with proven proficiency in building actionable dashboards/reports (e.g., Asana) and leveraging quantitative data to solve logistics challenges. Track record of driving mid-term and long-term process optimization and strategic CIPs rather than focusing strictly on daily operational firefighting. Demonstrated individual leadership, strong sense of ownership, and personal accountability to drive operational success without needing direct reports. Exceptional stakeholder management capabilities, with a track record of building cross-functional trust, influence, and credibility among peers and external partners while representing Logitech professionally. Solid financial acumen with experience in budget management, landed cost modeling, and freight audit support. Preferred Qualifications Experience with the practical application of AI in supply chain management or logistics. Proficiency in Project Management: PMP certified and project software skill user, specifically Asana. Master’s degree or relevant professional certifications (e.g., CSCP). Experience working in a fast-paced, high-volume global organization. Ability to work in a Dallas-based hybrid model (3 days/week commitment to WFO) Compensation: This position offers an annual base salary typically between $ 87,300 to 113,500 Logitech offers benefits such as Medical Coverage, Dental Coverage, Vision Coverage, Traditional and Roth 401(k) Plans, Flexible Spending Accounts, Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP), Basic and Additional Life Insurance, Disability Coverage, Adoption and Surrogacy Assistance, Tuition Reimbursement Plans, Commuter Benefits, Paid Time Off, Paid Holidays, Bereavement Leave, and Paid Parental Leave. title: Regional Business Unit Sales Specialist

The position works closely with Strategic, Key, and Regional Account Managers to engage customers, present technical solutions, and assist in closing opportunities. The role also supports technical presentations, webinars, and training sessions to promote the complete portfolio of transformer products. Key Responsibilities Sales Growth & Market Development Drive sales of Transformer products within the assigned region in alignment with BU strategic objectives. Identify, develop, and manage opportunities within the assigned customer segments Support key account managers with product-specific strategy, bid support, pricing guidance, and competitive positioning. Conduct business forecasting, territory pipeline review, and market planning with Sales leadership. Expand market share through new customer acquisition and strengthening relationships with existing accounts. Technical Sales Expertise Serve as the subject matter expert for the transformer product line, including test instruments, software solutions, and diagnostic platforms. Support account managers in technical discussions, product demonstrations, testing methodologies, and proof-of-concept engagements. Deliver advanced product presentations, webinars, trainings, and workshops tailored to customer needs. Provide application insights, measurement interpretation advice, and diagnostics to help customers evaluate testing results and outcomes. Work closely with BU leadership to communicate regional market conditions, customer requirements, competitive activity, and product feedback. Support the rollout of BU initiatives such as new releases, campaigns, positioning changes, or channel development activities Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner with Regional Sales teams, Product Management, Engineering, Marketing and Technical Support Assist in the creation and sharing of technical content, success stories, competitive comparisons, and market intelligence. Support operational alignment between BU and region to improve forecasting accuracy, supply planning, product focus, and sales success. Customer Engagement & Experience Conduct field visits with account managers and channel partners to engage customers face-to-face. Provide on-site testing support, troubleshooting guidance, and application advice when required. Ensure high customer satisfaction and strengthen Megger’s reputation as an industry leader in power transformer diagnostics and testing innovation. New Product Introduction (NPI) Support Lead regional product launches, ensuring market readiness through: Internal training Customer awareness campaigns Demonstration units Launch events and webinars Collect structured market feedback to support product refinement and roadmap development. Performance Indicators (KPIs) Regional revenue and growth of the Transformer portfolio. Opportunity pipeline development and conversion rates. Market share gain within strategic segments. Number of customer engagements, demos, and technical presentations delivered. Customer satisfaction and repeat business. Feedback and implementation of BU initiatives within the region. Internal competency improvement (sales team knowledge & capability). Strong technical understanding of transformer testing principles Proven ability to communicate and present complex technical concepts in a clear and structured manner. Experience working with utilities, OEMs, service companies, EPCs, or industrial customers. Desired Skills & Competencies Customer-focused, solution-oriented mindset. Strong commercial acumen with the ability to identify opportunities and close business. Ability to influence without direct authority in a matrix organization. Excellent presentation, training, and communication skills. Ability to travel at least 50% within the region.

title: Director, Product Management - Store Systems
jd_text: 7-Eleven is an iconic family of brands with over 86,000 locations, surpassing every retailer in the world. We revolutionize convenience, restaurants and fuel through cutting edge innovation — working hard to be the customer's first choice. 7-Eleven empowers our employees to "activate awesome" and make a meaningful impact in their stores and communities every day. If you're ready to grow, lead and make a difference, come join our team and help shape the future of convenience. Job summary The Director, Digital Product Management, owns the end-to-end product vision, strategy, and delivery for the technology platforms that power the 7-Eleven store. This leader is accountable for the full experience across our Retail Information System (RIS), back-office capabilities (7BOSS), operations innovation tooling, and the broader portfolio of in-store digital systems — ensuring every capability we ship makes it simpler and faster for franchisees and store associates to run a great store. This is a highly visible, cross-functional role that sits at the intersection of Digital, Operations, Merchandising, and Technology. The Director translates enterprise strategy and frontline needs into a clear, prioritized roadmap, and drives it from concept through adoption. Success is measured not by features delivered, but by the operational outcomes they create reduced labor burden in the store, faster and more accurate execution, higher franchisee satisfaction, and measurable business impact at scale across thousands of locations. The role leads a team of product managers and partners closely with engineering, design, UX research, and field operations to build a modern, scalable store systems platform — modernizing legacy capabilities while introducing new ones. The Director is expected to be the enterprise voice of the store: deeply grounded in how stores actually operate, rigorous about evidence and data, and persuasive with senior leadership on where to invest, what to retire, and how to sequence change so the field can absorb it. KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITES Look across product teams and feature sets with a focus on alignment and dependencies. Sets the overall product vision and strategies for the enterprise product by gaining a thorough understanding of customer and associate needs, both existing and potential, and using that knowledge to provide 7-Eleven customers and associates with an unparalleled shopping experience. Drives growth for the business by applying domain expertise to provide thought leadership and translating vision into action. Collaborates across the enterprise to create alignment between products in order to provide a seamless user experience. Understands financial and business impact of proposed product updates and activities within portfolio, prioritizes updates to support the enterprise roadmap, and based on prioritization allocates funding across the products. Identifies goals, metrics and appropriate analytics to measure the performance of the product and its individual features and continually makes recommendations and refinements to the product based on learnings. Contributes to and makes recommendations for strategic plans in support of key objectives in a timely and fiscally responsible manner. Participates in and influences development of technology roadmaps across the enterprise. Supports and nurtures strategic vendor relationships; recommends ways to influence vendors that align to domain, portfolio, and enterprise strategic objectives. Drives product development by reviewing performance and directing work efforts of product teams to ensure products are aligned with company, stakeholder and end user priorities. Understands enterprise goals and KPIs to ensure value is delivered against them. Resolves issues within or across product teams that may impair teams from delivery of a quality product in order to meet strategic, financial and technical goals. Receives and prioritizes incoming requests from business partners and stakeholders while keeping in mind the business strategy, product vision and user needs. Provides guidance on design of products while keeping in mind dependencies and integration with other products across the enterprise. Reviews and analyzes product metrics to inform strategic and tactical product decisions. Make suggestions that help drive operational excellence to create internal customer satisfaction and meet operational metrics. Provides leadership, mentoring and coaching to Product Managers. Attracts, retains and develops top talent to build a world class Product Management Team. Conduct annual and mid-year reviews, reviewing individual development plans and providing performance feedback. Fosters collaboration with team members (Engineering, UX, etc.) to drive value and identify and resolve impediments. Acts as a proponent of modern software development practices. Advocates for the end user and stakeholder by becoming associated with the product, empathizing with and understanding user needs. Works with the product team to continuously assess progress, disseminate lessons learned, and understand next steps. Manages cross functional team and stakeholder expectations to execute on product strategy and provides education to requestors to determine prioritization based on tangible benefits and/or user experience. Guides more junior team members in strategy, alignment, analysis and execution tasks. Participates in and contributes to learning activities around modern software design and development core practices. Experience 10+ years of experience in product management, with a strong background in consumer-facing and internal platforms. Proven success delivering products in retail tech domains (eCommerce, wallets, mobile apps, delivery services). Experience with store technology and back-office systems is a strong plus. Demonstrated ability to lead and grow cross-functional teams with direct and indirect reporting lines. Strong understanding of customer-centric design, UX research, and agile delivery methodologies. Familiarity with data tools and analytics for decision-making. Key Skills Required Brick-and-Mortar Experience is highly desired: Understanding of the retail spaces including Point of Sales, Back Office, Associate Enablement and Store Insights Digital Experiences for Customers & Store Employees: Digital retail platforms, omnichannel strategies, and customer experience. Product Management Excellence: Proven track record in product strategy, roadmap development, and lifecycle management. Agile & Lean Methodologies: Hands-on experience with agile development, scrum, and lean startup principles. Data-Driven Decision Making: Ability to leverage analytics, A/B testing, and customer insights for product decisions. Stakeholder Management: Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills for managing senior leadership and cross-functional teams. Team Leadership: Experience building and leading high-performing product teams at scale. Change Management: Ability to drive organizational change and digital transformation. Problem-Solving: Strong analytical and creative problem-solving skills for complex business challenges. Experience with product discovery frameworks (Design Thinking, etc). Exposure to modern tools for roadmap planning, experimentation, and user feedback management. Exposure to a Franchising model is highly desired. Education Bachelor’s degree required; concentration in Business, Technology, or a related field preferred. jd_text: As a team member in Finance at Nationwide, a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales, the opportunities are endless! Let Nationwide help create your career journey!
